subject: ent
title: Tonsils and adenoids

steps.tx: **Acute tonsillitis** is viral in most cases; bacterial (group A streptococcus) likelihood rises with Centor features: fever, tonsillar exudate, tender anterior cervical nodes and absence of cough (age adjusted McIsaac). Antibiotics (penicillin patterns) are for likely streptococcal, severe or high risk cases, preventing rheumatic fever in at risk populations, not shortening most viral illness. Infectious mononucleosis (EBV) mimics with fatigue, splenomegaly, atypical lymphocytes and amoxicillin rash, forbidding contact sports while spleen enlarged.
steps.say: Fever, pus, nodes, no cough scores strep. Mono plus amoxicillin erupts in rash; swollen spleen bans rugby.

steps.tx: **Peritonsillar abscess (quinsy)** collects between tonsil capsule and superior constrictor in young adults after tonsillitis: severe unilateral sore throat, trismus, drooling, muffled hot potato voice, uvula deviated away and bulging soft palate. Needle aspiration or incision drainage plus antibiotics and fluids treats most; airway vigilance precedes procedures, CT only for atypical, deep or paediatric concerns. Interval tonsillectomy debate follows recurrence and severity patterns individually.
steps.say: One sided agony, jaw locked, uvula pushed over: quinsy. Drain it, guard airway.

steps.tx: Recurrent tonsillitis surgery uses frequency thresholds (Paradise pattern: seven episodes in one year, five yearly for two years, or three yearly for three years, documented and disabling) balanced against natural resolution and surgical harms (bleeding about 2 to 5 percent spectrum, anaesthetic, pain). **Adenoid hypertrophy** obstructs growing children causing mouth breathing, hyponasal speech, snoring sleep apnoea, glue ear contribution and adenoid facies in chronicity; adenoidectomy indications centre obstruction and selected recurrent otitis or sinusitis pathways.
steps.say: Seven, five, three: Paradise counts for tonsillectomy. Big adenoids block noses, ears and sleep.

steps.tx: **Key point.** Tonsil cancer red flags rewrite sore throat care: unilateral tonsil enlargement or ulcer, referred otalgia (glossopharyngeal), neck mass, weight loss in adult smoker or drinker suggests squamous carcinoma (HPV positive oropharyngeal rising in younger non smokers with cystic level II node). Any persistent unilateral tonsil asymmetry in adult needs urgent cancer pathway examination and biopsy or tonsillectomy histology, never repeated antibiotics. Post tonsillectomy bleed returns to theatre when significant: primary under 24 hours (reactionary), secondary at 5 to 10 days (infection slough).
steps.say: One big ulcerated tonsil in adult is cancer until histology clears it. Day seven bleed after tonsillectomy returns urgently.
